subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be denied from patching legacy ownerless session rows, rather than retaining a compatibility path that permits an installed plugin to adopt or mutate those rows?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes existing persisted-row behavior at a plugin authorization boundary; source and proof establish the technical behavior, but only maintainers can decide whether fail-closed protection outweighs compatibility for pre-ownership rows.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, keep non-plugin operator management unchanged, and land this focused security repair before reconciling the sibling creation-path PR.

options.title: Require an explicit migration design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a narrowly owned doctor or migration path for legacy plugin-created rows rather than allowing runtime adoption.

options.title: Preserve legacy plugin mutation
options.body: Keep ownerless rows patchable by plugin-runtime callers, accepting the cross-plugin ambiguity that the patch is designed to remove.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, keep non-plugin operator management unchanged, and land this focused security repair before reconciling the sibling creation-path PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The current head includes this contributor’s fixup and the decision concerns the authorization/compatibility policy of the gateway session surface.
